newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: South Korea to boost investment in Britain.
newsitem.headline: South Korea to boost investment in Britain.

text.p: South Korea is planning a big increase in its direct investment in Britain, President Kim Young Sam told Prime Minister Tony Blair on Monday, according to British officials.
The two leaders, who held a 25-minute meeting on the fringes of a U.N. environmental summit, also agreed that Britain's Queen Elizabeth would visit South Korea in 1999, the officials said.
Kim told Blair his country "intended to increase its investment tenfold in the next few years" to between $4 billion and $5 billion.

South Korean officials were not immediately available to confirm Kim's remarks, which British officials took as a robust expression of confidence in the British economy, or to elaborate on the investment totals.
It was not clear whether Kim was including in his projected total a big semiconductor plant that LG Group is building in south Wales at a total cost of 1.1 billion pounds.
